html:
The Anmatyerr are an Aboriginal people of Central Australia, in the Northern Territory north of Alice Springs. They speak one of the Upper Arrernte languages.

Their neighbours were the Warlpiri to the west, the Kaytetye to the north and the Alyawarr to the east. In the 1870s the Overland Telegraph Line was built through their country, and cattle stations followed.

In 1928, after a dingo trapper was killed, police and settlers killed many Anmatyerr, Warlpiri and Kaytetye people in the Coniston massacre, one of the last large frontier killings in Australia.

Anmatyerr artists are among the best known in Australian art. Clifford Possum Tjapaltjarri painted at Papunya, and Emily Kame Kngwarreye began painting in her late seventies at Utopia and became famous worldwide. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
